root_cause: A member removed from a group keeps its local overlay and MLS state (removal only drops them from the tree). On re-invite, accepting the new Welcome hit joinIdempotent, which saw the group id already held and either short-circuited onto dead state or threw 'already exists'; the invitation then ended as 'no longer valid' and the member could not chat.
fix: A held group is treated as stale iff our own leaf is absent from its tree or its state cannot be read (welcomeSubscription isHeldGroupStale / staleLocalGroup.isLocalGroupStale). For a stale group the Welcome is pre-validated (readPreJoinGroupData), then under the join lock: live subscription teardown with bounded waits that fail closed (replaceTeardown, EpochResolver.disposeAndDrain, retired dispatcher/ingest drains), seen-id clear, destroy, shared purge (leaveGroupImpl.purgeGroupLocalData), join, resubscribe. A localStorage recovery marker keeps the invitation retryable across repeated post-destroy join failures and reloads (InvitationRetryableError -> 'Joining failed. Please try again.'). Nothing is published by the replace path.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Each adversarial round found a further async path (live ingest, retired dispatcher, retired ingest waiter, retired setup) that could write MLS state after destroy; MarmotContext's subscription lifecycle has no single owner of 'all outstanding work for group X', so teardown completeness had to be proven path by path. Remediation was capped after round 5 with the last path filed as a backlog finding.
retrospective.surprised_by: marmot-ts dispose() is a flag, not a drain: an ingest already in its state save completes after dispose, so destroy-then-rejoin needs an explicit await of resolver work.
lead_clarifications: Stale rule narrowed to own-leaf-absent OR unreadable state (Welcome epoch ignored); flagged for owner confirmation.
